subject: English Language
name: Basic 1 English Language
description: The Basic 1 English Language curriculum focuses on developing foundational skills in listening, speaking, reading, and writing. It adopts an integrated, thematic approach to help learners acquire effective communication skills, appreciate values, and develop core competencies like critical thinking and collaboration.

strands.title: Oral Language (Listening and Speaking)
strands.description: Developing listening and speaking skills through songs, rhymes, storytelling, dramatisation, conversation, and presentation.

subStrands.title: Songs
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding of a variety of songs.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding of a variety of songs

indicators.description: Listen to and sing familiar songs with appropriate expressions

exemplars.description: Let learners identify some familiar songs.
Let learners sing familiar songs and clap, tap and or dance to the rhythm.
Let learners answer a variety of questions on the songs.
Discuss the moral lesson in the songs with learners.

subStrands.title: Rhymes
subStrands.description: Appreciating a variety of literary pieces through rhymes and tongue-twisters.

contentStandards.description: Appreciate a variety of literary pieces

indicators.description: Listen to and recite rhymes and tongue-twisters with accompanying actions

exemplars.description: Have learners recite familiar rhymes.
Introduce new rhymes by performing them.
Lead learners to echo-read the rhymes.
Let learners recite the lines in groups/pairs and as individuals, as they tap or clap to the rhythm.
Guide learners to identify rhyming words and teach the accompanying actions.
Note: Recycle the rhymes in the next few days for learners to memorise them.

subStrands.title: Story Telling
subStrands.description: Responding to stories, identifying characters, and retelling stories.

contentStandards.description: Respond to stories

indicators.description: Listen to stories and be able to identify characters with their roles

exemplars.description: Mount appropriate story pictures.
Guide learners to tell the story logically, using the pictures at each stage.
Pause and show pictures for learners to ask questions or answer questions to predict the next stage.
Let learners retell the story in a chain, using the pictures, if necessary.
Tell learners your personal response and guide them to do same. e.g. i. Why do you like the story? ii. I like the story because... iii. Which part do you like best? iv. I like where...

indicators.description: Retell short stories

exemplars.description: Show pictures to guide learners to retell a story told in class.
Let learners follow the pictures to retell the story logically/sequentially.
Let learners tell other stories they know.
Let storyteller pause for others to sing any appropriate song.

subStrands.title: Dramatisation and Role-Play
subStrands.description: Performing stories through dramatisation.

contentStandards.description: Perform stories

indicators.description: Dramatise stories heard

exemplars.description: Begin the lesson with the narration of a familiar story.
Have learners identify the characters in the story and their roles.
Have learners role-play some specific characters in groups.
Let learners talk about theirs and others' roles.

subStrands.title: Conversation
subStrands.description: Talking about Oneself, Family, People, Places, Greetings, Customs, Events, Social/Cultural Values, Manners and other Themes.

contentStandards.description: Use certain culturally acceptable language for communication

indicators.description: Use appropriate greetings for different times of the day

exemplars.description: Revise daily greetings by having learners identify greeting times in the day. e.g. Morning-Good morning, Afternoon-Good afternoon, Evening-Good evening.
Discuss the correct responses to these greetings.
Let learners take turns to demonstrate greetings at different times of the day and also practise the appropriate responses.
Discuss the importance of greetings.

indicators.description: Describe the home, people or places

exemplars.description: Welcome children and have them sit in a semi-circle. Greet them and introduce the topic for discussion. Use the Community Circle Time Strategy.
Learners are provided with an opportunity to interact freely with the teacher and peers, starting with greetings.
Have learners use appropriate responses and non-verbal language (body language and facial expression) as they greet each other.
Show pictures of homes, people and places and have learners think-pair-share their observation with the person sitting next to them and with the class.

indicators.description: Talk about their school and places in the school

exemplars.description: Use the Community Circle Time Strategy.
Show pictures of their school and places in the school (the library, the computer lab, the headmaster's office, the playing field etc.)
Have learners think-pair-share ideas/views about the pictures in pairs and then with the large group.
Have learners talk about the activities that go on in these places and their importance to the individual.

indicators.description: Use a wide variety of words to describe different situations and events

exemplars.description: Use a conversational poster on different situations/events.
Have learners think-pair-share, looking at the various illustrations on the poster.
Have them use expressions learnt and other new ones to describe the situations and events.
Have learners, working in groups, role-play the situations and events on the poster.

contentStandards.description: Use culturally acceptable language for communication (Engagement)

indicators.description: Engage in collaborative conversation

exemplars.description: Let learners, working in groups, talk about some common places in the school (e.g. canteen, head teacher's office, library, etc.).
Lead learners, with questions, to talk about the places and their importance.
Let learners identify the importance of the places listed above.
In pairs/small groups, let learners engage in conversations on specific topics.

indicators.description: Talk about likes and dislikes: food, animals, toys, etc.

subStrands.title: Listening Comprehension
subStrands.description: Using appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts.

contentStandards.description: Use appropriate skills and strategies to process meaning from texts

indicators.description: Listen to and reproduce narrative texts

exemplars.description: Before Reading: Activate the previous knowledge of the learners by making them think-pair-share with their friends, the cover illustrations and pictures accompanying the story. Have them predict the story.
During Reading: Read a story. Pause at vantage points and have learners talk about the content of the text.
After Reading: Have the learners answer simple questions based on the text. Have them role-play the events in the story.

indicators.description: Recognise and relate the sequence of events in a narrative text

exemplars.description: Read a narrative text aloud to learners.
Put learners in pairs/groups to identify and talk about the parts of the story (e.g. beginning, middle and ending).

indicators.description: Recognise and discuss characters in a story

exemplars.description: Read a story aloud to learners.
Have them discuss, in pairs/small groups, the main and minor characters in the story.
Have groups/pairs share their views with the whole class.

indicators.description: Listen to and produce descriptions of pictures and objects (e.g. vehicles, animals)

exemplars.description: Show pictures of common objects and animals to learners.
Have learners think-pair-share what they see in the picture.
Have them describe, in groups/pairs, the pictures to one another in turns.

subStrands.title: Asking and Answering Questions
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in asking and answering questions.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in asking and answering questions

indicators.description: Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering Yes/No questions

exemplars.description: Demonstrate Yes/No questions and their responses.
Drill learners on the questions and responses.
Let pair of learners ask and answer questions, e.g. Pupil A: Is this a book? Pupil B: Yes, it is / No, it isn't.

indicators.description: Use appropriate pronunciation and intonation in asking and answering Wh-questions

exemplars.description: Revise Yes/No questions.

Let learners identify some objects in the class (e.g. board, bag, chair, etc.) and use them in asking simple questions, e.g. Should I clean the board? Is that your chair? Do you have a pencil in your bag?
Introduce Wh-questions in context. e.g. i. What is this? ii. What is your name? iii. How old are you? iv. How are you?
Pair learners to ask and answer questions.
Note: Yes/No questions use rising intonation and Wh is falling intonation. However, answers for both use the falling intonation.

subStrands.title: Giving and Responding to Commands, Instructions, Directions and Making Requests
subStrands.description: Demonstrating understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate understanding in commands, instructions, directions and requests

indicators.description: Give and respond to commands and instructions

exemplars.description: Give commands and instructions to learners. e.g. Command: Keep quiet. Hands up. Sit down. Bring your books. Start work, etc.
Pair learners to give/obey commands.
Have learners listen to simple instructions and act in response.

Let learners practise by giving commands in pairs, etc. e. g. Instructions: Draw a circle. Draw a triangle in the circle. Draw a square in the triangle. Response: [Learners draw according to instructions]

indicators.description: Make and respond to polite requests using the word "Please"

exemplars.description: Demonstrate knowledge of requests and their responses. Let learners respond to requests using; yes, ok, etc.
Pair with learners to take turns to make and respond to polite requests. e.g. Please give me your pencil. A: May I use your pen? B: Yes/No. Let them change roles.

subStrands.title: Presentation
subStrands.description: Planning and presenting information and ideas for a variety of purposes.

contentStandards.description: Plan and present information and ideas for a variety of purposes

indicators.description: Identify audience and purpose of presentation

exemplars.description: Have learners to do "show and tell" to introduce a friend to his/her parents at his/her birthday party.
Create more scenarios for learners to introduce their friends. Note: Introduce expressions like "Hello, meet my Dad", etc.

indicators.description: Generate and select ideas on a given topic for presentation e.g. My father, My friend, etc

exemplars.description: Introduce the activity and as learners listen and observe, talk about the topic, e.g. "My friend". Briefly discuss your presentation.
Let learners take turns to talk about their friends.
Encourage others to ask questions after each presentation.

indicators.description: Speak with confidence before different audiences, e.g. small group, class, etc

exemplars.description: Have learners draw members of their nuclear family.
Through think-pair-share strategy, let learners show and talk about their family members in pairs, smaller groups and as a class.
Use probing questions to have learners talk more about their family members. e.g. i. Who is this one? ii. Why did you draw him or her first? Encourage shy learners to speak.

strands.title: Reading
strands.description: Developing reading skills through pre-reading activities, phonics, word families, vocabulary, comprehension, and fluency.

subStrands.title: Pre-Reading Activities
subStrands.description: Understanding text concepts and manipulating sounds.

contentStandards.description: Know how a text works for reading and writing

indicators.description: Handle books appropriately

exemplars.description: Have learners Think-Pair-Share the reasons for keeping books neat and handling them well.
Lead learners to make some rules to guide the handling of books.
Demonstrate how to handle books, e.g. holding it, turning a book, opening the pages properly, etc.
Discuss the information on the cover and title pages with learners, e. g. What can you find on the cover? The title, Author, Illustrations and illustrators, etc.
Call learners in turns to demonstrate how to handle books, e.g. opening a book, holding a book, etc.
Let learners, in groups, role-play how to handle books, e.g. keeping them neat.

contentStandards.description: Manipulate the sounds of the letters of English

indicators.description: Orally blend two or three sounds together to make one syllable word, e.g. (a-sh = ash, b-i-n = bin)

exemplars.description: Make individual sounds and have learners blend them together to make one-syllable words, e.g. (a-sh = ash, b-i-n = bin, a-t = at, a-m = am, i-n = in, c-o-t = cot).

indicators.description: Orally segment spoken syllables/words into individual sounds e.g. stop = s-t-o-p

exemplars.description: Model segmenting spoken syllables/words into individual sounds, e.g. (stop = s-t-o-p, am = a-m, pot = p-o-t).
Provide opportunities for learners to practise segmenting syllables/words into individual sounds.

indicators.description: Say the new word when asked to delete, add initial sound or substitute an initial, middle or final sound (Phoneme deletion, addition, substitution)

exemplars.description: Say a word and model using phoneme deletion, addition and substitution strategies to say new words from the given word, e.g. phoneme deletion: brat - rat, etc.; phoneme substitution: cat - bat, bat - bet, bet - bell, etc.; phoneme addition: all - ball, etc.

subStrands.title: Phonics
subStrands.description: Connecting sounds to letters and blending them to read and write.

contentStandards.description: Connect sounds to letters and blend letters/syllables in order to read and write

indicators.description: Identify the alphabet in order

exemplars.description: Introduce the lesson with alphabet songs paying attention to the letters as they sing.
Show an alphabet chart and have learners identify the letters of the alphabet (aA- zZ).
Use alphabet cards, alphabet trees, picture cards, etc. to play alphabet games.
Let learners play matching games with the cards, e.g. Sound Ball Game, Find My Partner, etc.

indicators.description: Recognise and produce letter names and sounds randomly

exemplars.description: Have learners play alphabet games to practice recognition of letter names at random. e.g. Lucky Dip game, Treasure Hunt.
Let learners use letter cards to order the letters of the alphabet.
Have learners find out which letter comes before the other, among a given set of letters, as a whole class, in groups, in pairs and individually.
Select letters whose sound you intend to teach, e.g. two letters at a time.
Say each sound first in context and then in isolation, e.g. ants-a.
Have learners repeat it after you.
Give examples of words that contain each sound at the initial, medial and final positions, e.g. bag, table, bulb.
Have learners work in pairs to provide examples of words that contain the sounds.

indicators.description: Understand the relationship between spelling of words and sounds of speech

exemplars.description: Blend vowel sounds with consonant sounds to produce words, e.g. am, at.
Let learners segment the sounds in the words and blend them by using blending games.
Ask learners to give examples of words.
Write the words and have learners sound the individual letters and blend them to produce words.
Have learners work in pairs/groups to further practise sound segmentation and blending to produce the words.

indicators.description: Blend sounds to produce simple syllables/words and blend syllables to produce words

exemplars.description: Blending sounds: Clap the syllables of common words. e.g. table, pencil, pen, book, boy, girl, etc.
Let learners clap the syllables of words after teacher.
Put learners into groups/pairs. Distribute letter cards to the groups.
Demonstrate blending using letter cards, e.g. f-a-n = fan, b-a-g = bag, b-e-d = bed, p-e-n = pen.
Use learners' words to build a vocabulary chart and encourage them to go round to read.
Blending syllables: Have learners use think-pair-share to come out with single syllables and blend them to form words, e.g. sis + ter = sister.
Let the pairs present their words and guide them by using the words to form two-word or three-word sentences. e. g. My sister is happy.

indicators.description: Segment syllables/words into sounds

exemplars.description: Revise the sounds of letters and words learners have learnt.
Demonstrate syllable segmentation by breaking two-syllable words into syllables. e.g. pencil = pen-cil, baby = ba-by, mother = mo-ther.
Let learners read the words and use them in sentences.

indicators.description: Use alphabetic knowledge to decode known words

exemplars.description: Let learners sing an alphabet song.
Put them into groups and write sentences containing some new words for learners to decode by segmentation. e.g. This is a mango. This is my sister.
Have learners read similar words from the word charts.

subStrands.title: Word Families, Rhyming Endings and Common Digraphs
subStrands.description: Using rhyming endings and digraphs to enhance reading comprehension.

contentStandards.description: Employ knowledge of rhyming endings to enhance reading comprehension

indicators.description: Use common rhyming endings to decode simple words

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to simple word formation using the phonic slide to change the sound at the initial, medial and final positions of words, e.g. pat, mat, fat.
Have learners build on these rhyming endings.
In groups, let learners read out their words.
Have learners form sentences with these rhyming words.

subStrands.title: Vocabulary
subStrands.description: Understanding word meanings and usages.

contentStandards.description: Understand word meanings and usages

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate sight words and use many of them in meaningful sentences

exemplars.description: Introduce the appropriate sight words beginning with the commonest. Write them on the board, e.g. chair, table, child, etc.
Use the word "tree" to teach the sight words.
Have learners repeat the words aloud.
Have learners use the sight words in meaningful sentences.
Tell a story and have learners identify sight words in the story. Have learners use the sight words in meaningful sentences, e.g. determiners - the: The boy is my friend.

indicators.description: Ask questions to find out the meaning of new words

exemplars.description: As learners listen carefully, tell a story twice.
Let learners answer questions based on the story.
Have them mention words they hear in the story.
Let learners tell the meanings of some of the words.
Have learners make their own simple sentences using the key words.

indicators.description: Use words acquired through talk and reading in conversation

exemplars.description: In groups, let learners engage in conversation using familiar and high frequency words on given topics. e. g. My Classroom.

subStrands.title: Comprehension
subStrands.description: Understanding texts read using skills and strategies.

contentStandards.description: Understand texts read

indicators.description: Use illustrations, text clues (title, headings) and context to make inferences and predictions

exemplars.description: Let learners use illustrations, text and context clues to make predictions before, during and after reading to enhance comprehension of text.

indicators.description: Ask and answer factual and inferential and applicative questions about level-appropriate texts

exemplars.description: Have learners read level appropriate texts independently, with minimal support from peers/teacher.
Encourage them to ask and answer factual and inferential questions about the texts to enhance comprehension.

indicators.description: Retell level-appropriate texts in own words

exemplars.description: Use the Simple Herring Bone strategy to guide learners to retell the story in their own words. (when? what? who? how? why?)

contentStandards.description: Use knowledge skills and techniques of reading to understand

indicators.description: Demonstrate understanding of the purpose and features of narrative texts

exemplars.description: Use examples of short and simple texts to guide learners to understand the purpose and features of narrative texts.
Have learners identify the different purposes in different narrative texts read/heard.
Have them identify the features of given texts in pairs or in groups.

indicators.description: Describe characters and their actions in a story

exemplars.description: Put learners in groups to identify and describe characters and their actions in stories read.

indicators.description: Connect, ideas and information in stories to own experiences and knowledge of the world

exemplars.description: Tell/read out texts.
Let learners answer simple questions based on the events, characters and values, etc. in the text.
Have them relate ideas and information in the stories to personal experiences and knowledge of the world.

indicators.description: Read level-appropriate texts with prompting and support

exemplars.description: Have learners read texts with all the prompting and support that can help them in their reading.

indicators.description: Use a variety of comprehension-strategies e. g prediction before reading a text, cover page, etc

exemplars.description: Begin the comprehension lesson with before reading activities that develop and activate the background knowledge of learners. e.g. K of KWL (What learners know about the topic of information text, prediction using pictures, title, treatment of vocabulary, etc.).
Continue with while reading activities to enhance their understanding of the text. e.g. Herring Bone strategy (what? who? when? how? why?) or W of KWL (What the learners want to know).

End the lesson with after reading activities that help learners to organize their ideas, remember the story, use the information acquired from the text and relate it to their daily lives, e.g. answering questions, retelling the story in their own words, learners linking story to their everyday life experiences etc.

indicators.description: Identify the structure of a story e.g. beginning part, middle and the end

exemplars.description: Narrate a suitable story.
Have learners identify the structure of the story by recalling what happened at the beginning, middle and ending.

subStrands.title: Fluency
subStrands.description: Reading texts with good speed, accuracy, and expression.

contentStandards.description: Read texts with good speed, accuracy and expression

indicators.description: Read short and simple sentences at good pace

exemplars.description: Teacher models reading at a reasonable pace.
Have learners read short and simple sentences at a reasonable pace.
Let learners read in small groups.

indicators.description: Recognise one hundred and twenty sight words including content words

exemplars.description: Have learners go over the sight words they have learnt during the period.
Let learners echo-read simple texts.
Let learners play vocabulary games for vocabulary consolidation, e.g. Lucky Dip game, Pick and Say, Word Hunt.
Have learners make simple meaningful sentences with the sight words.

strands.title: Writing
strands.description: Developing writing skills through pre-writing, penmanship, labelling, sentence construction, and simple compositions.

subStrands.title: Pre-Writing
subStrands.description: Developing muscular control and hand-eye coordination.

contentStandards.description: Write patterns for muscular control and hand-eye coordination

indicators.description: Make given patterns, trace and draw various objects

exemplars.description: Demonstrate vertical, horizontal and oblique strokes/patterns. e.g. /// \\\ |||
Let learners write these strokes/patterns in the air.
Have learners write them in their books.
Note: If need be, learners may first make these strokes by tracing and/or joining dots. Ensure correct sitting posture and correct grip of the writing tool.

indicators.description: Model various objects of interest

exemplars.description: Use papers to model an object as learners observe.
Let learners, in their groups, choose and model different objects.
Let learners tell the name of the object and what it can be used for.

subStrands.title: Penmanship/Handwriting
subStrands.description: Copying and writing letters correctly.

contentStandards.description: Copy and write letters of the alphabet correctly

indicators.description: Copy letters of the alphabet clearly

exemplars.description: Introduce learners to the lines and spaces they will be expected to write in.
Demonstrate the letter on the board and in the air several times.
Give ample practice. Let learners practise writing in the air, on sheets of paper or in jotters.
Let learners execute the writing task.
Give feedback after assessing learners' work.

subStrands.title: Writing Letters - Small and Capital
subStrands.description: Using skills to write legibly and boldly.

contentStandards.description: Use general skills strategies and knowledge of letter sounds to write legibly and boldly

indicators.description: Match lower and upper case letters

exemplars.description: Show a chart of letters (small and capital). e.g. ABCDE... abcde...
Place letter cards (small and capital letters) on teacher's table.

Put learners into groups and ask representatives of the groups to take turns to pick and match the letter cards to the letters on the chart. Those who are able to match them correctly win points for their groups and receive stars.
Let learners write the letters in their books.

indicators.description: Copy the names of objects correctly in both upper and lower case letters

exemplars.description: Let learners go round and observe labelled objects in the classroom.
Let learners go with their books and change sitting positions to enable them copy the names of the objects.
Let learners sit in groups to edit their work.
Have them share their work by exchanging their books with other groups to appreciate one another's work.

indicators.description: Write words using both capital and small letters

exemplars.description: Write words in upper and lower cases.
Model pronunciation of target words for learners to repeat.
Let learners copy the words from the board.
Encourage learners to space out letters appropriately in the words. Let group leaders help other learners (who are not able to write some letters correctly).

subStrands.title: Labelling Items
subStrands.description: Drawing and labelling simple objects.

contentStandards.description: Draw and label simple objects

indicators.description: Draw simple pictures of peers or various objects and use invented spelling to write about oneself

exemplars.description: Have a picture of a friend or anybody and write at least three lines about the person. Paste this in a corner of the class. Have a chart of various objects labelled (e.g. objects at home in, the environment etc.) and post them on the walls of the classroom.
Have learners go round to observe the pictures.
In groups, let learners share their observations.
Ask learners to draw and label three objects of their choice.
Have each learner choose and draw a peer and write a line or two about that person.
Assist learners with spelling where necessary.
Have learners share their work with their partners. Similarly, let learners draw pictures of themselves and write a sentence or two about them.

subStrands.title: Writing Simple Words and Sentences
subStrands.description: Writing words and sentences correctly.

contentStandards.description: Write words and sentences

indicators.description: Make a list of objects in the school

exemplars.description: Guide learners with questions to talk about the various areas or places in the school e.g. head teacher's office, canteen etc.
Put learners into groups. Let each group choose a name for their group and an area or place they want to work on.
Let each group list the objects found in the place of their choice.
Have a big chart on the wall and copy their lists on the chart. Let groups take turns to edit their work.
Let learners copy the edited words into their books.

indicators.description: Write simple familiar words

exemplars.description: Let learners mention their favourite dishes or food.
Let learners select one food and talk about the ingredients used in its preparation, e.g. Jollof.
Let learners mention the ingredients as teacher writes them on the board.
Let them then work as individuals, choose their own special food or dish and write the ingredients.
Let learners do peer editing.

indicators.description: Use basic descriptive words in writing simple sentence

exemplars.description: Have learners identify objects in the classroom, e. g. tables, chairs, bags, etc.
Let learners tell the sizes, shapes and colours of the objects. Explain simply to them that the words talk about objects.
Have learners work in pairs to write simple sentences, describing objects in the classroom, e. g. My classroom is big. The board is long and white. The doors and windows are big.
Encourage learners to write two simple sentences each (Exceptional learners should write four simple sentences).

subStrands.title: Controlled Writing
subStrands.description: Writing simple compositions.

contentStandards.description: Write simple compositions

indicators.description: Find, read and copy sentences from a given substitution tables

exemplars.description: Have a simple 3-4 column substitution table on the board.
Have learners identify the words that make up the table.
With examples, guide learners to form oral sentences from the substitution table.
Have learners write their sentences.
Ask pairs to do peer editing.
Invite learners to read out their sentences to the class for feedback.

indicators.description: Write a simple composition using a substitution table

exemplars.description: Write a simple and short composition in a substitution table and have learners copy this out.
Using Think-Pair-Share, have learners read their compositions.

indicators.description: Match parts of sentences to compose meaning texts

exemplars.description: Demonstrate the activity.
Have learners rearrange jumbled parts of sentences to make meaningful texts.
Let learners read their sentences to the class for feedback.

subStrands.title: Descriptive Writing
subStrands.description: Demonstrating knowledge of description in writing.

contentStandards.description: Demonstrate Knowledge of description in writing

indicators.description: Use words and simple sentences to describe self

exemplars.description: Model describing yourself in 2-3 simple sentences using simple descriptive words.
Write some descriptive words and discuss them with learners.
Through questions, have pairs of learners describe themselves to each other. e.g. What is your name? My name is... How old are you? I am...
Assist learners to write out their sentences.

strands.title: Using Writing Convention/Grammar Usage
strands.description: Applying grammar rules and conventions in writing.

subStrands.title: Using Capitalisation
subStrands.description: Applying capitalisation rules.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of capitalisation in writing

indicators.description: Write capital letters correctly

exemplars.description: Through pick and write activity, revise writing of capital letters with learners.

indicators.description: Use capital letters at the beginning of titles and names of people

exemplars.description: Demonstrate knowledge of capital letters and invite individuals to write names with capital letters on the board.
Assist learners to write their names. Let them begin with capital letters, e.g. Kofi, Ama, Samuel, Sule.
Lead learners to write titles of people. e.g. Mr Badu, Mrs Darko.

indicators.description: Use capital letters to write other proper nouns

exemplars.description: Let them write the names of towns and particular places they are familiar with, beginning with capital letters, e.g. names of schools, Adukrom Primary School.

subStrands.title: Using Action Words
subStrands.description: Applying knowledge of action words in communication.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of action words in communication

indicators.description: Use the present tense of verbs to describe habitual actions

exemplars.description: Introduce the activity and tell learners two things you do daily.
Put learners in groups to talk about the things they do everyday: e. g. I wash my face every morning.
Write the two things you do in two simple sentences and read it out to learners.
Have each learner write two of the habitual things they do. You may assist them with spelling.
Invite each of them to present their work to the class for the class to react to the presentations.

indicators.description: Use the present tense of verbs to express the present state of things or situations

exemplars.description: Introduce the activity and demonstrate it.
Guide learners with questions to describe the state of given things or situations, e.g. My bag is red.

indicators.description: Use the present tense continuous form of verbs

subStrands.title: Using Qualifying Words - Adjectives
subStrands.description: Using adjectives to describe people and objects.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of adjectives in communication

indicators.description: Identify adjectives and use them to describe self and other people

exemplars.description: Have learners read level-appropriate texts describing people.
Put learners in groups to discuss the texts read. Provide questions to help them identify the descriptive words.
Have learners write simple sentences to describe themselves, using the descriptive words identified.
Have learners write parallel sentences to describe their friends.

subStrands.title: Using Simple Prepositions
subStrands.description: Using prepositions to indicate position.

contentStandards.description: Apply knowledge of prepositions in communication

indicators.description: Identify and use prepositions in oral and written language to indicate position

exemplars.description: State the position of various classroom objects using simple prepositions.
Give sample sentences (on sentence cards) to learners. e.g. Mary is in the room. Aba is sitting on the chair.
Let learners identify the words in, on, etc. as words that show position.
Pair up learners and have them use the prepositions identified in simple and meaningful sentences.
Let each learner write two sentences describing the position of objects in the classroom.

subStrands.title: Spelling
subStrands.description: Using phonics to spell simple words.

contentStandards.description: Use phonics knowledge to spell words

indicators.description: Identify and spell simple words correctly

exemplars.description: Help learners to write two letter words correctly e. g. go, so, in, on.
Using word cards, help learners to write three letter words correctly, e. g. see, low, bow.

indicators.description: Fill in blank spaces in simple words

exemplars.description: Provide a passage with blank spaces and help learners to fill in the gaps or spaces with familiar two or three letter words.

strands.title: Extensive Reading
strands.description: Building a culture of reading for pleasure and information.

subStrands.title: Building the Love and Culture of Reading
subStrands.description: Encouraging independent reading habits.

contentStandards.description: Read widely for pleasure and demonstrate independent reading and learning in the literary area

indicators.description: Read a variety of age - appropriate books and texts from print

exemplars.description: Using book tease or book talk, introduce the reading/ library time.
Have a variety of age appropriate books for learners to make a choice from.
Introduce picture or wordless books, pop-up and flip-the-page texts to learners.
Encourage them to read individually and in pairs, and provide support and encouragement.
